name: io.github.code0xff/1gateway
title: 1gateway
description: Pay-per-call MCP tools for agents via x402 USDC: Korean data, onchain, crypto, web and AI tools.

tools.name: kr_company_report
tools.description: Use when an agent needs an English due-diligence brief on a South Korean company. Input: business_number, dart_corp_code, stock_code or q (exact name); format=json|markdown; news=true|false. Output: JSON summary, business overview, annual financials (revenue, profit, debt, YoY), major shareholders, procurement, DART events (90 d), risk, sanctions, data gaps, sources. AI-written; not advice. Use instead: kr_company_profile for the profile only; kr_supplier_check for a quick vetting. Example: ?stock_code=005930 (output example is illustrative) Price: $0.50 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

q.description: Company name (Korean or English), matched exactly after removing legal-form words

format.description: markdown adds a readable English Markdown rendering of the same report

news.description: Include up to 5 recent third-party news headlines (default true)

tools.name: kr_apartment_trades
tools.description: Use when you need actual apartment sale prices in a South Korean district for a month (property research, valuation, comps). Data: MOLIT (Korea land ministry) reported deals since 2006, updated daily. Input: region (5-digit LAWD_CD, e.g. 11680 Gangnam-gu), month (YYYYMM). Output: JSON trades with contract date, complex (Korean + romanized), area m2, floor, build year, price in KRW and USD, price per m2, deal type, cancelled flag. Use instead: kr_apartment_trades_summary for count, median/average and size-class stats only. Example: ?region=11680&month=202609 Price: $0.0045 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

region.description: 5-digit 시군구 code (LAWD_CD), e.g. 11680 = Seoul Gangnam-gu, 11110 = Jongno-gu, 41135 = Seongnam Bundang-gu. Unknown codes → 400 (not charged).

month.description: Contract month YYYYMM, 200601 to the current month (KST)

tools.name: kr_apartment_trades_summary
tools.description: Use when you need a quick housing-market snapshot for a South Korean district-month instead of raw trades. Data: MOLIT reported apartment sales, cancelled deals excluded. Input: region (5-digit LAWD_CD, e.g. 11680), month (YYYYMM). Output: JSON count, median and average price and price per m2 in KRW and USD, min/max price and median price per pyeong in KRW, breakdown by size class, top complexes by volume. Use instead: kr_apartment_trades for each transaction row (comps). Example: ?region=11680&month=202609 Price: $0.0045 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

region.description: 5-digit 시군구 code (LAWD_CD), e.g. 11680 = Seoul Gangnam-gu. Unknown codes → 400 (not charged).

month.description: Contract month YYYYMM, 200601 to the current month (KST)

tools.name: kr_bok_ecos_series
tools.description: Use when you need official Bank of Korea statistics (base rate, money supply, key indicators) as a time series. Input: stat (ECOS table code, e.g. 722Y001), cycle (A/S/Q/M/SM/D), start, end (period format of cycle), optional item (e.g. 0101000). Output: JSON series with table/item names, units, observations [{period,value}] (max 1,000 rows). Only BOK-authored tables are served. Example: ?stat=722Y001&cycle=M&start=202401&end=202412&item=0101000 Price: $0.0045 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

stat.description: ECOS statistic table code, e.g. 722Y001 (base rate). Non-BOK tables → 403 (not charged).

cycle.description: A annual, S semi-annual, Q quarterly, M monthly, SM semi-monthly, D daily

start.description: Start period in ECOS format (A: YYYY, Q: YYYYQn, M: YYYYMM, D: YYYYMMDD)

end.description: End period, same format as start

item.description: Item code 1 (e.g. 0101000). Optional item2..item4 also accepted.

tools.name: kr_law
tools.description: Use when you need the official text of a South Korean statute, decree or rule, or one article of it. Statutes only: no court decisions or personal data. Input: q (statute name in Korean, e.g. 근로기준법) or mst (law serial no.), optional article (e.g. 2), limit (articles, 1-100, default 30). Output: JSON law metadata (ministry, effective date), articles [{label,title,text}] in original Korean, official URL, attribution. Example: ?q=근로기준법&article=2 Price: $0.0045 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

q.description: Statute name in Korean (exact name preferred), e.g. 근로기준법. Required unless mst is given.

mst.description: 법령일련번호 (law serial number) from a previous answer

article.description: Single article number, e.g. 2 or 제2조

limit.description: Max articles when no article is given (default 30)

tools.name: macro_treasury_curve
tools.description: Use when an agent needs the official US Treasury par yield curve for a day or a recent stretch. Input: optional date (YYYY-MM-DD, default latest), days (1-366 history ending at date). Output: JSON yields per tenor (1m to 30y, percent), 2s10s and 3m10y spreads in bp, inversion flags, change over the range, history. Weekend or holiday dates fall back to the prior business day. Example: ?days=5 Price: $0.003 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

date.description: Curve date YYYY-MM-DD (default latest published; no curve that day → previous business day)

days.description: Business days of history ending at date (default 1)

tools.name: kr_weather_forecast
tools.description: Use when you need the official weather forecast for a point in South Korea for the next ~3-5 days. Data: KMA (Korea Meteorological Administration) village forecast on a 5 km grid, issued 8 times a day. Input: lat, lon (WGS84 decimal; Korea only). Output: JSON hourly then 3-hourly temperature C, sky, precipitation type and probability %, rain and snow amounts, humidity %, wind; plus daily min/max. Example: ?lat=37.5665&lon=126.978 Price: $0.0045 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

lat.description: Latitude, WGS84 decimal degrees (KMA domain ≈ 32–44; outside → 400, not charged)

tools.name: kr_public_holidays
tools.description: Use when you need South Korea's official public holidays for a year (business-day calculation, scheduling, settlement and payroll calendars). Data: KASI (Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute) special-day register, incl. substitute and temporary holidays once promulgated. Input: year (YYYY, 2004-2100). Output: JSON list with date, weekday, Korean and English name, isPublicHoliday, kind. Use instead: time_business_days for business-day math. Example: ?year=2026 Price: $0.0027 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

tools.name: kr_trade_exports_10day
tools.description: Use when you need South Korea's earliest export read: the Korea Customs 10-day provisional release (days 1-10, 1-20, full month; out on the 11th, 21st and 1st). Input: optional month (YYYYMM) and period (10, 20, full); default latest. Output: JSON exports in USD with YoY %, latest 10-day increment, 10 key items (semiconductors, cars, ships...) and 10 markets (China, US, EU, Vietnam...) with YoY and share, next release date. Use instead: kr_trade_pulse for one-call summary with a 12-month trend; kr_trade_hs for one product by HS code. Example: ?month=202609 Price: $0.0045 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

month.description: Release month YYYYMM (default: latest release; from 201701)

period.description: 10 (days 1-10), 20 (days 1-20) or full; requires month. Default: latest available for the month

tools.name: kr_trade_hs
tools.description: Use when you need South Korea's monthly trade for a product by HS code (e.g. 8542 chips, 870323 cars, 2710 petroleum). Data: Korea Customs Service, finalized monthly. Input: hs (2-10 digit prefix), optional month (YYYYMM, default latest), limit (1-100), sort (exports, imports, balance, total). Output: JSON totals (exports FOB, imports CIF, balance in USD, kg) with YoY % and 10-digit HSK lines with English HS descriptions and YoY. Use instead: kr_trade_exports_10day for the earliest 10-day totals. Example: ?hs=8542&month=202608 Price: $0.0045 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

hs.description: HS code prefix, 2-10 digits (e.g. 8542 integrated circuits, 870323 passenger cars)

tools.name: kr_trade_pulse
tools.description: Use when you need a one-call read on South Korea's export cycle for macro, FX or chip-sector analysis. Data: Korea Customs 10-day and monthly releases. Input: none. Output: JSON headline (latest exports and YoY, semiconductor share, strongest/weakest item and market, 3-month average YoY, momentum), latest release by item and market, 12 monthly export totals with YoY, and HS 8542 integrated-circuit trade for the latest month. Use instead: kr_trade_exports_10day for one release in detail; kr_trade_hs for one product by HS code. Example: /v1/trade/pulse Price: $0.0045 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

tools.name: kr_company_resolve
tools.description: Use when an agent must identify a South Korean company before looking up its profile or public-procurement record. Input: one of business_number (10 digits), dart_corp_code, stock_code (KRX, e.g. 005930) or q (company name, exact match ignoring 주식회사/(주)/spacing); first wins. Output: JSON companies with stable companyId, Korean and English names, stock code, DART code, match type, ambiguous flag. Data: OpenDART, KONEPS. Use instead: kr_company_profile for the profile after resolving; kr_company_report for a full brief in one call. Example: ?stock_code=005930 Price: $0.002 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

q.description: Company name (Korean or English), matched exactly after removing legal-form words

tools.name: kr_company_profile
tools.description: Use when an agent needs a normalized profile of a South Korean company for KYB, research or sales. Input: id (companyId from /v1/kr/company/resolve). Output: JSON profile: names, business/corporate/DART/stock ids, market, KSIC code, founding date, fiscal year end, address, homepage, KONEPS supplier registration. No CEO names. DART data is a weekly snapshot of KRX-listed companies (asOf in response). Data: OpenDART, KONEPS. Use instead: kr_company_report for a full report with financials and filings; kr_business_status for only open/closed tax status; kr_supplier_check for a pass/fail vetting. Example: ?id=kr-dart-00126380 Price: $0.0045 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

tools.name: kr_company_procurement
tools.description: Use when an agent needs a South Korean company's government contract wins for sales, credit or competitor research. Input: id (companyId) or business_number; optional from/to (YYYY-MM-DD, max 92 days, default last 90 days), category (goods,works,services,foreign), min_amount, limit, offset. Output: JSON summary (award count, total and largest KRW, top agencies) and awards with title, agency, amount, date. Data: KONEPS. Use instead: kr_company_profile for company basics. Example: ?id=kr-dart-00126380 Price: $0.009 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

id.description: companyId from /v1/kr/company/resolve; give id or business_number

business_number.description: Business registration number; give id or business_number

from.description: Bid opening date from (default: 90 days before to; range at most 92 days)

category.description: Comma list of goods, works, services, foreign (default all)

min_amount.description: Only awards of at least this many KRW

tools.name: kr_business_status
tools.description: Use when an agent must check that a South Korean business is still operating before paying, contracting or onboarding it (KYB). Input: b_no (1-20 business registration numbers, comma-separated, hyphens ok). Output: JSON per number: status (active, suspended, closed, unregistered, or no_answer: unknown, registered null), VAT taxpayer type, closure date, tax-type change and e-invoice dates, companyId. Data: NTS, synced every 30 min. Use instead: kr_supplier_check for a combined vetting; kr_company_profile for company details. Example: ?b_no=1248100998 Price: $0.002 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

b_no.description: Business registration numbers (사업자등록번호), 10 digits each, comma-separated (max 20); invalid check digit → 400, not charged

tools.name: kr_address
tools.description: Use when an agent must normalize or translate a South Korean address (shipping, checkout, KYC forms). Input: q (Korean address or part of one, e.g. road name + number or neighborhood + lot number), optional limit (1-5). Output: JSON matches with official road-name and lot-number addresses in Korean and English, postal code, building name, admin and road codes. Data: Ministry of the Interior road-name address API. Example: ?q=테헤란로 152 Price: $0.002 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

q.description: Korean address or part of it (2+ chars; at most 40 Korean characters; no SQL words or % = > < [ ]); bad input → 400, not charged

tools.name: kr_filings
tools.description: Use when an agent needs recent material disclosures of a South Korean listed company (rights offerings, CBs, buybacks, M&A, litigation, earnings, periodic reports). Input: corp (DART corp_code, KRX stock code or kr-dart- id) or q (exact name), optional days (1-365, default 30); or date (YYYY-MM-DD, KST). Output: JSON list with rceptNo, date, Korean title, English type label, DART link. Summaries: /v1/kr/filings/summary. Use instead: kr_filing_summary for one filing explained in English. Example: ?corp=005930&days=90 Price: $0.0045 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

corp.description: DART corp_code (8 digits), KRX stock code (6 characters) or kr-dart-<corp_code>

q.description: Company name (Korean or English), matched exactly after removing legal-form words

date.description: Receipt date (KST); with corp, only that day (inside the days window). No filings that day/window → count 0, not an error

tools.name: kr_filing_summary
tools.description: Use when an agent needs a Korean corporate disclosure in English. Input: rcept_no (14-digit DART receipt number from /v1/kr/filings). Output: JSON with headline, what_happened, key_figures (amounts, ratios, share counts with units), parties, key_dates, why_it_matters, confidence, original Korean title and DART link. Machine-generated paraphrase, not the official text. Unknown rcept_no or model outage is refused before payment. Use instead: kr_filings for finding the rcept_no. Example: ?rcept_no=20261030801383 Price: $0.02 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

tools.name: kr_supplier_check
tools.description: Use when an agent must vet a South Korean supplier or counterparty before paying, contracting or onboarding it. Input: one of business_number, dart_corp_code, stock_code or q (exact company name). Output: JSON summary (riskLevel, riskFlags such as closed/suspended or sanctions match, per-section status) plus NTS status, DART profile, 90-day KONEPS award summary and OFAC/EU/UK screening of the English name. Not a legal determination. Use instead: kr_business_status for tax status only; kr_company_report for a full report; kyb_check for non-Korean companies. Example: ?stock_code=005930 Price: $0.015 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

q.description: Company name (Korean or English), matched exactly after removing legal-form words

tools.name: web_metadata
tools.description: Use when an agent needs to know what a URL is before reading it, or to build a link preview or citation. Input: url (public http/https). Output: JSON with final URL after redirects, HTTP status, content type, title, description, site name, language, canonical, preview image, favicon, Open Graph and Twitter tags, RSS/Atom feeds, hreflang alternates, JSON-LD types, robots, first H1. No JavaScript is run. Use instead: web_read for the page text; site_profile for security headers, DNS and domain age. Example: ?url=https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/ Price: $0.002 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

url.description: Public http(s) URL; private/internal addresses → 400 (not charged)

tools.name: domain_lookup
tools.description: Use when an agent must check a domain: does it resolve, who hosts its DNS and mail, is email authenticated, how old, when it expires. Input: domain (URLs accepted). Output: JSON DNS records (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, TXT, CAA, SOA), mail provider, parsed SPF and DMARC, DNS provider, and RDAP registration (registrar, created, expires, age in days, status, DNSSEC). Failed lookups → null + dnsErrors; all failed → 503. No contact data. Use instead: site_profile for the page and security headers too; email_check for one email address. Example: ?domain=google.com Price: $0.0045 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

domain.description: Public domain or hostname (punycode for IDNs, e.g. xn--...); a URL is reduced to its hostname. Internal/reserved names → 400 (not charged)

tools.name: fx_rates
tools.description: Use when you need an official daily FX rate or currency conversion (USD, EUR, KRW, JPY, CNY, GBP + 24 more). Input: base (default EUR), optional symbols (comma list), date (YYYY-MM-DD, last ~90 days; weekends use the prior fixing), amount. Output: JSON rates for the fixing date, % change vs prior fixing, converted amounts, raw ECB EUR rates. Source: ECB statistics, updated each TARGET day ~16:00 CET; reference only. Use instead: fx_convert for converting an amount, or a date older than ~90 days; fx_history for a daily series or period stats. Example: ?base=USD&symbols=KRW,JPY&amount=100 Price: $0.002 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

base.description: Base currency, ISO 4217 (one of the 30 ECB reference currencies; default EUR)

date.description: Fixing date YYYY-MM-DD within the last ~90 days (default latest)

amount.description: Amount in base currency to convert

tools.name: fx_convert
tools.description: Use when you need to convert an amount between currencies (USD↔KRW, EUR→JPY, ...) at the official ECB reference rate, today or on a past date. Input: from, to (1–10 comma-separated), amount (default 1), optional date (YYYY-MM-DD since 1999-01-04; weekends use the prior fixing). Output: JSON per target rate, inverse rate and converted result, the fixing date used. Source: ECB statistics; reference only. Use instead: fx_rates for every ECB rate for one fixing with % change vs the prior fixing; fx_history for a date range. Example: ?from=USD&to=KRW,JPY&amount=250 Price: $0.002 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

from.description: Source currency, ISO 4217 (one of the 30 ECB reference currencies)

tools.name: fx_history
tools.description: Use when you need a historical exchange-rate series or a period summary (e.g. USD/KRW over the last quarter). Input: symbols (1–10), base (default EUR), start and end (YYYY-MM-DD since 1999-01-04; default last 30 days; max 366 days). Output: JSON daily series of ECB fixings, and per currency first/last, % change, min/max with dates, average and daily volatility. Source: ECB statistics; reference only. Use instead: fx_rates for one fixing (latest); fx_convert for converting one amount. Example: ?base=USD&symbols=KRW,JPY&start=2026-07-01&end=2026-09-30 Price: $0.002 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

start.description: Start date YYYY-MM-DD (default end minus 30 days; earliest 1999-01-04)

end.description: End date YYYY-MM-DD (default today; range ≤ 366 days)

tools.name: time_convert
tools.description: Use when scheduling across time zones or turning a local time into UTC without guessing DST. Input: to (IANA zones or KST, PST, CET...), optional from (zone of a local time, default UTC), time (ISO 8601, Unix seconds, or now). Output: JSON UTC instant, Unix time, and per zone: local ISO time with offset, weekday, abbreviation, DST and business-hours flags, day difference. Use instead: time_overlap for meeting slots; time_business_days for working-day math. Example: ?time=2026-10-12T09:00&from=Asia/Seoul&to=America/New_York,Europe/London Price: $0.002 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

to.description: 1–25 target zones, comma-separated (IANA names like Asia/Seoul, UTC, or abbreviations like KST, PST, CET)

from.description: Zone of the input local time (default UTC; ignored when time has an offset)

tools.name: time_overlap
tools.description: Use when scheduling a meeting across time zones. Input: zones (2-10, IANA or KST/PST/CET), date, work_start/work_end (default 09:00-18:00), include_weekends. Output: JSON overlap windows in UTC and every zone's local time, top 3 one-hour slots ranked by distance from each zone's day edges, partial windows when no full overlap, next DST change per zone. Use instead: time_convert for converting one instant. Example: ?zones=America/New_York,Europe/London,Asia/Seoul&date=2026-11-03 Price: $0.002 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

zones.description: 2–10 time zones, comma-separated; the first is the anchor whose local date is scanned

date.description: Meeting date YYYY-MM-DD in the anchor zone (default today UTC)

work_start.description: Local start of working hours, HH:MM

work_end.description: Local end of working hours, HH:MM

tools.name: time_business_days
tools.description: Use when computing due dates, SLAs, settlement or delivery dates. Input: start date, then days (add -260..260 business days) or end (count business days between), optional country KR, US, GB, DE, FR or JP for public holidays (omit = weekends only). Output: JSON result date or business/calendar day counts, holidays skipped on the way, holiday scope. Use instead: kr_public_holidays for the Korean holiday list. Example: ?start=2026-12-22&days=5&country=US Price: $0.003 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

days.description: Business days to add (negative = go back); give days or end (days wins if both)

end.description: Count business days from start (excluded) to end (included), at most 2 years apart; ignored when days is given

country.description: Public holiday calendar (omit for weekends only)

tools.name: site_profile
tools.description: Use when an agent must vet or research a website in one call (lead research, security or SEO check, is this site legit). Input: url or bare domain. Output: JSON page metadata, HTTP status, HTTPS and HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect, server and hosting hints, 7 security headers, robots.txt (sitemaps, AI-crawler rules), llms.txt presence, plus domain DNS, mail provider, SPF/DMARC and RDAP registrar, age and expiry. Use instead: web_audit for a graded score with fixes; web_check for only up/down and latency; domain_lookup for DNS, mail auth and registration only (no page fetch). Example: ?url=stripe.com Price: $0.009 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

url.description: Site URL or bare domain (https:// assumed); private/internal targets → 400 (not charged)

tools.name: web_check
tools.description: Use when an agent must know if a URL is up before linking, scraping or alerting. Input: url or bare domain (https:// assumed). Output: up (final status < 400, or 401/403/407/429 with accessRestricted: true), HTTP status, final URL, redirect chain (max 8), HTTPS and http-to-https upgrade, response time in ms, content type, server. Down or timed-out sites return up: false. Private targets → 400 before payment. Use instead: site_profile for a full site profile; web_screenshot for how the page looks. Example: ?url=example.com Price: $0.002 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

url.description: URL or bare domain (https:// assumed); private/internal targets → 400 (not charged)

tools.name: watch_create
tools.description: Use when an agent must be told when something changes. Input: type (price, balance, stablecoin_transfer, filing, insider_trade, hl_position, sanctions, web_status), target, condition, days 7-30, optional webhook. Output: id, one-time secret, poll URL. Checked every 5-60 min; events by poll or HMAC-signed webhook. $0.002/day ($0.004 web_status), paid once. Best-effort, no SLA; not refunded. Use instead: agent_webhook for receiving third-party webhooks. Example: POST {"type":"price","symbol":"ETH","below":2000} Price: $0.014–$0.12 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

type.description: What to watch. Without type the request is a price probe (402 at the 7-day minimum)

days.description: Watch length in days, 7-30 (default 7); price = days × daily rate

symbol.description: price: one ticker (BTC, ETH, SOL, …; DEX-priced like /v1/crypto/price)

above.description: price/balance: fire when the value rises above this (USD for price, token units for balance); give above or below, not both

below.description: price/balance: fire when the value falls below this

address.description: balance: wallet (0x…); hl_position: Hyperliquid account (below= liq. distance %); sanctions: any crypto address; stablecoin_transfer: optional from/to filter

chain.description: balance: base, ethereum, arbitrum, monad; stablecoin_transfer: ethereum, base, arbitrum

token.description: balance: token symbol from the default set (e.g. USDC) or NATIVE (default); any change fires when no above/below

corp.description: filing: Korean company (DART corp_code, stock code or kr-dart- id) instead of ticker

side.description: insider_trade (ticker/cik): new Form 4 open-market buy, sell or both (default)

url.description: web_status: site (checked every 15 min)

webhook.description: Optional https URL (port 443, public host) for signed POSTs: header x-1gateway-signature t=…,v1=HMAC-SHA256(key=hex(SHA-256(secret)), `${t}.${body}`)

tools.name: agent_inbox
tools.description: Use when an agent must receive email: sign-up codes, magic links, or ongoing mail. Input: days (1 default, 7, 30). Output: address @inbox.1gateway.dev, id, one-time secret, read and extend URLs. Reads are free (header x-inbox-secret): sender, subject, text, codes and confirmation links extracted. Receive only; 20/50/200 messages, 256 KB each, attachments dropped; mail kept 30 days. Extendable. Use instead: agent_webhook for HTTP callbacks; email_check for checking an address. Example: GET /v1/agent/inbox?days=7 Price: $0.01–$0.1 per call, paid in USDC (Base, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) via x402.

days.description: How long the address lives: 1 (default, $0.01), 7 ($0.03) or 30 days ($0.1)

tools.name: agent_webhook
